name: Middle Ear Neuroendocrine Tumor
aliases: Neuroendocrine Adenoma of the Middle Ear

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Middle Ear Neuroendocrine Tumor

criteria.description: Presence of neuroendocrine tumor cells with organoid, trabecular, or glandular patterns on histopathology
Positive immunohistochemical staining for neuroendocrine markers such as chromogranin, synaptophysin, and cytokeratin
Imaging evidence of a well-circumscribed mass localized to the middle ear without bone destruction
Symptoms consistent with a middle ear mass such as conductive hearing loss and tinnitus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of neuroendocrine tumor cells with positive immunohistochemical staining for neuroendocrine markers
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of metastatic neuroendocrine tumors from other primary sites.

searchTerms: hearing loss in one ear due to conduction

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; rare cases may show elevated serotonin or chromogranin A if functional
imaging: CT scan showing well-defined middle ear mass without bone erosion
MRI demonstrating isointense to hypointense lesion on T1 and hyperintense on T2 with contrast enhancement
genetic: No known recurrent genetic mutations; molecular studies limited
other: Histopathology revealing neuroendocrine tumor cells with positive chromogranin and synaptophysin staining

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of keratinizing squamous epithelium and bone erosion
Histology shows purely glandular epithelial cells
History of primary neuroendocrine tumor elsewhere
Imaging and biopsy consistent with metastasis

redFlags: Evidence of bone destruction or intracranial extension on imaging
references: Ferlito A, et al. Neuroendocrine tumors of the middle ear: a review. Head Neck Pathol. 2013.
Marinelli JP, et al. Middle ear neuroendocrine tumors: clinical and pathological features. Otol Neurotol. 2017.
